native_mechanisms: A stone on a corner = a distance declared final and never reconsidered (permanently settled set).
A duck carries a spool whose length is the running sum of all road lengths crossed to reach it (tentative additive distance labels, relaxed by predecessor sum + edge weight).
Each round, sweep all unstoned corners to find the single leader duck with the shortest carried thread and settle it before any other duck moves (linear-scan extract-min of the frontier).
Threads toward dead-end houses (no outgoing/useful far side) hang slack and are thrown away unspooled, never measured again (prune edges into already-final or useless vertices).

Before trusting the leader, trace its thread back shuttle-by-shuttle to the source, re-adding each road's centimetres, and only stone it if the traced total matches the written one (predecessor-chain re-verification of the min label).
core_technique: Dijkstra's algorithm over a CSR graph with a linear (AVX2/OpenMP-vectorised) array scan extract-min over a swap-compacted active set — i.e. the classic O(n^2) no-heap Dijkstra variant, plus a cheap predecessor-chain re-sum sanity check that is a no-op in practice.
